raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Someone added a gc.collect() supposedly for reclaiming GPU memory allocated for dequantized tensors. However, I am unable to reproduce any excess GPU memory allocation that is recovered by this gc.collect, any dequantized tensors created in NVRx code are deleted when code returns from NVRx. Additionally, the check only tests for fp8, but misses other conditions where quantization may occur, e.g., fp4.

Dropping this gc.collect() saves about about 30% of the total exposed time (including finalize) as measured by telemetry data. This overhead never showed up in the logs as it was not measured by the timers.

detail.title: Drop the FP8-only gc.collect() after checkpoint saves

files.patch:
@@ -4378,13 +4378,6 @@ def save_checkpoint_and_time(
                 report_memory(f"(after save_checkpoint for iteration {iteration})", process_group=dp_gtp_remat_group)
         num_checkpoints_memory_reported += 1
 
-        if args.fp8:
-            # Run garbage collection after checkpoint saving to free memory from
-            # dequantized bf16 tensors that were temporarily created during fp8
-            # model checkpoint saving.
-            with _otel_managed_span('checkpoint', 'megatron.checkpoint.gc_collect', is_goodput_span=True):
-                gc.collect()
-
         # timers.log reports min & max across ranks -> a collective. Sitting right
         # after the per-rank-imbalanced save (and outside the save spans), it's a
         # prime spot for the fast ranks to serialize waiting for the slowest saver.
